c0cc2e75c87aacd7:
Write tests as methods in a test class. A test method is an instance method whose name begins with test, takes no parameters, and returns void. For example, TestColorsRed calls project code and uses assertion APIs to report when it does not produce the expected result. A function might return an unexpected value, or an inappropriate method call might throw an exception. See XCTest Assertions for these cases.
Import the correct headers into the test class so the methods can access the code under test.
Xcode runs each method independently. Each must therefore prepare and clean up its supporting variables, structures, and objects that interact with the target API. If every test method shares the same setup or cleanup, put it in the setup and teardown instance methods, which always run. See Test Class Structure.
